headline: Northbeam is moving fast and turning that into production work, and they asked how to reach Global Premier, so answer with a joint financial services plan and named banking accounts.
evidence: Production deployments: 41 in the last 12 months (19 in the last 2 quarters), against 15 needed for Preferred. Their certifications are turning into live deployments, at about 5.1 certified people per deployment.
Usage on partner-led customers rose from 100 to 390 over 3 quarters (+62% last quarter). Claude engagements are up 85% vs. the prior 2 quarters, and Claude is 45% of their AI book.

They need less help from us: Applied AI support hours fell from 120 to 80 per quarter while their book grew, now about 2.8 hours per engagement. The AE noted their architects needed almost no help on the second banking deal.
Deal registrations went from 9 to 31 per quarter with a 48% win rate, so the registrations are converting. Only 1 of 12 open pilots has stalled (8%).
At the 2026-10-08 QBR they asked to co-build a financial services practice on Claude and asked what Global Premier takes. They are opening a Singapore office in Q1.
caveats: Claude's share is 45% of an estimated AI book of about 140 engagements, so the share figure is only as good as that estimate. Our notes logged 1 competitor mention in the last 90 days, with no detail, so it is worth asking who it was. The momentum index of 60 is backed up by production and usage, not pulled up by one noisy input. Still, part of the momentum comes from certifications growing 50% in a quarter, and that pace may not continue. Global Premier is a multi-quarter goal, and if we set expectations too high the conversation could backfire. We have only two notes, both upbeat.
who: Partner manager (Dana Ruiz) + financial services sales lead
goal: Agree a draft joint business plan for a Claude financial services practice, with named target banking accounts and dated milestones toward Global Premier.
agenda: Walk through the Global Premier gap: 790 more certified people, 59 more production deployments, 9 more public stories, a third region (Singapore/APAC), and a joint business plan.
Pick 3 to 5 named banking accounts to co-sell, building on the two banking deals from this quarter.
Agree what investment we offer (co-sell coverage, funding, help turning banking wins into public stories) and what Northbeam commits in return.
Set the APAC launch milestones around the Q1 Singapore opening, and ask about the competitor mentioned in the last 90 days.
tier_outlook: Northbeam meets every Preferred requirement with room to spare (210/100 certified, 41/15 deployments, 6/3 stories), so there is no risk at the 2026-10-31 review. Global Premier is not realistic at this review. At current growth, with a Singapore office in Q1, it is a believable 12 to 18 month goal if a joint business plan is agreed.

headline: Halvorsen & Pike's global AI CoE has made a competitor its default for agentic builds, and the drop is already in the numbers. Get our executive sponsor in front of their global decision-makers this week to win back a defined slice of agentic work before the 31 October tier review.
evidence: Claude engagements fell 26% (140 in the last 2 quarters vs 190 in the 2 before). Claude is only 7% of their roughly 1,900 AI engagements.
Usage on partner-led customers fell 7% last quarter (98 to 91), 9% over 3 quarters. Deal registrations fell from 40 to 19, down 32% last quarter alone. Momentum index is -16.
Only 18 production deployments in the last 2 quarters against 160 in the trailing 12 months, so deployments have slowed sharply. 14 of 30 open pilots have stalled for 90+ days (47%).
Applied AI support hours rose 11% to 510 (6.9 hours per Claude engagement) while output fell. Their delivery teams are using our engineers on pilots they should run themselves (PM note, 27 Aug).

3 Oct PM note: their CoE now defaults to a competitor for agentic builds, a pricing and tooling call made at the global level. 18 Sep AE note: we lost 2 joint pursuits where they proposed the competitor stack. 9 competitor mentions in 90 days. Q3 QBR postponed twice.
caveats: The 12-month totals (160 deployments, 1,385 certified people, 17 public stories) still look strong. They lag and hide the decline, so don't read the tier cushion as health. Certifications are flat (+0% last quarter), so the 1,385 figure reflects past investment, not current commitment. The CoE decision comes from one call note: it is the CoE lead's account of a global decision and may be firmer or softer than it sounds. The data doesn't show whether a joint business plan, required for Global Premier, is in place and current. The estimated AI book of about 1,900 engagements is an estimate, so the 7% share is approximate. Claude still has a real foothold in document-heavy workflows, so this is a narrowing of what they use us for, not a full exit yet.
who: Partner manager (Marcus Lee) + our executive sponsor / partnerships VP, meeting their global AI CoE lead and the alliance exec who owns the pricing and tooling decision
goal: A written commitment from their global CoE to put Claude back on the approved default list for agentic builds, with a named set of joint pursuits to test it on, backed by an agreed fix for the pricing and tooling objections.
agenda: Get the specific pricing and tooling gaps behind the CoE's default decision, and what would reverse it
Review the 2 lost joint pursuits and the 14 stalled pilots, then agree which pilots to revive or close
Cap Applied AI hours and replace them with a skills plan so their delivery teams can run pilots themselves
Confirm the joint business plan is current ahead of the 31 Oct review, and reschedule the twice-postponed QBR
tier_outlook: They clear every Global Premier threshold with room to spare: 1,385 certified people vs 1,000 required, 160 deployments vs 100, 17 public stories vs 15, 3 regions vs 3. They should keep the tier at the 31 Oct review as long as the joint business plan, which isn't shown in the data, is in place. The risk is at the following review. With only 18 deployments in the last 2 quarters, their 12-month count will fall toward or below 100 as the stronger older quarters drop out of the window. The tier is safe on paper now but will erode if agentic work stays with the competitor.

headline: Meridian is a small partner going all-in on Claude, with growth turning into real production work. Help get their second public story approved and agree a plan to reach Preferred.
evidence: Claude is 65% of their AI work (30 of ~46 engagements in the last 2 quarters), and Claude engagements are up 150% on the prior 2 quarters.

Usage on partner-led customers has climbed every quarter (100 → 180 → 310 → 520), up 68% last quarter. They have 9 production deployments in 12 months, 6 of them in the last 2 quarters, 7 open pilots and none stalled.

Certifications are turning into delivery: 34 certified people for 9 deployments (3.8 per deployment). Their deal registrations win 55% of the time over 12 months, and the AE says 3 of their last 4 closed.
They need less help from us as they grow: Applied AI support hours fell from 40 to 22 per quarter (-27% last quarter), now 1.7 hours per Claude engagement.

Partner manager note (Oct 2): Silverline's CTO credits Meridian's architecture workshop. Meridian wants to package it as a repeatable logistics offering and asked how to get a second public story approved.
caveats: They joined in April 2026 and start from a small base, so the percentage growth looks bigger than the absolute numbers (11 deal registrations, 9 deployments). The momentum index of 82 is backed up by every input, not pulled up by one noisy number. Their total AI book (~46 engagements) is an estimate, so the 65% share is approximate. The evidence comes from just two notes, both positive, and the logistics focus depends on one flagship customer (Silverline). Falling support hours could also mean they're under-asking for help on harder deployments, though no stalled pilots suggests not.
who: Partner manager (Marcus Lee) + partner marketing for the customer story
goal: Leave with a date to submit the Silverline public customer story and a written plan to reach Preferred by the following tier review: +66 certified people, +6 production deployments, +2 public stories.
agenda: Silverline story: what approvals are needed, who owns each step, target date to submit
Turn the logistics architecture workshop into a packaged offering, plus 2–3 named target accounts for co-selling
Preferred gap plan: which of the 7 open pilots can reach production, and a certification ramp from 34 to 100
Third story candidate from recent deployments
tier_outlook: They comfortably clear Select on every requirement (34/10 certified, 9/2 deployments, 1/1 story), so there's no risk at the Oct 31 review. They won't make Preferred at this review: they're short 66 certified people, 6 production deployments and 2 public stories. At the current pace (certifications up ~80% a quarter, about 3 deployments a quarter), Preferred looks reachable within 2–3 quarters. Public stories are the bottleneck most worth unblocking now.

headline: Quarry is committed to Claude but can't get pilots through customer security and architecture review. Agree a plan to build production-architecture capability at Quarry before our Applied AI hours rise further.
evidence: Pilots are stuck: 9 of 15 open pilots have stalled for 90+ days (60% stall rate), and only 1 production deployment came in the last 2 quarters
Partner manager note (Oct 6): pilots stall at the customer's security/architecture review, and Quarry's certified people are mostly developers with no one who can design for production
Our Applied AI support hours rose every quarter (60 → 95 → 140 → 180, +29% last quarter), about 8.4 hours per Claude engagement, so we are doing the work Quarry can't
AE note (Sep 29): a customer in a Quarry pilot came to us directly because the Quarry team was stuck
Commitment is real: Claude is 32% of their AI book and Claude engagements grew 9% vs the prior 2 quarters. Usage is flat (+1% over 3 quarters), so the problem is capability, not intent
caveats: The 32% share and the 120 AI engagements are estimates. The two notes are single conversations, and the security review gap is the partner manager's read, not confirmed with Quarry. The 2 competitor mentions in the last 90 days aren't explained. If they point to Quarry steering stalled pilots to another vendor, this becomes a Rescue. Certifications stopped growing at 31 after an early jump, which could mean training effort has stalled. A momentum index of -2 shows them as flat, but it doesn't capture the stalled pilots or the growing support burden.
who: Partner manager (Priya Shah) + Applied AI lead
goal: Quarry commits to a named production/security architecture lead and a dated plan to take 3 stalled pilots through customer security review. Our Applied AI hours move from doing their delivery work to coaching that lead.
agenda: Go through the 9 stalled pilots and pick the 3 closest to production
Name a Quarry architect and enroll them in architecture/security enablement, with a reference architecture and security review pack
Agree how Applied AI support works from here: we coach on the 3 pilots, we stop doing their delivery, and we set an hours cap
Ask about the 2 recent competitor mentions and the customer who came to us directly
tier_outlook: Select is safe at the Oct 31 review: 31 certified (10 needed), 3 production deployments in the last 12 months (2 needed), 1 public story (1 needed). Only 1 deployment came in the last 2 quarters, though. If older deployments drop out of the 12-month window without new ones, Select would be at risk at the next review. Preferred is far off: they are short 69 certified people, 12 production deployments and 2 public stories. That isn't realistic until the production gap is fixed.

headline: Brightwater is a small partner that does almost all its AI work on Claude, and it is one certification and one public story away from Select. Help it finish both before the 31 Oct tier review.
evidence: Claude is 86% of their AI book (19 of ~22 AI engagements in the last 2 quarters), and Claude engagements are up 36% on the prior 2 quarters
Usage on partner-led customers rose every quarter (100→140→190→260), up 37% last quarter and 160% over 3 quarters
Certifications turn into production: 2 production deployments in the last 12 months from 9 certified people (4.5 per deployment), 4 open pilots and none stalled
Deal registrations are small but they close: 1→1→2→3, with a 67% win rate over 12 months
Partner manager note (9 Oct): 'One more certification gets them to Select'. Their customer is willing to do a public story, and they asked how approval works
caveats: The numbers are small, so the percentage changes and the momentum index (38) look bigger than they are. One lost pilot would change the picture. A public story may not get through approval in 8 days, so they could miss Select at this review for process reasons, not because of commitment. Applied AI support hours fell 20% (from 10 to 8). That probably means they need less help, but it could also mean less engagement. All the qualitative read comes from one call note.
who: Partner manager (Priya Shah), plus whoever owns customer story approval in partner marketing
goal: Agree a plan, with an owner and a date, to get the 10th certification done and the customer story submitted for approval in time for the 31 Oct Select review. If the story can't make it, agree that it gets credited at the next review.
agenda: Name the person taking the 10th certification and set the exam date this week
Explain the public story approval process and timeline, and start the submission with their willing customer
Decide what happens if approval runs past 31 Oct (interim review or credit at the next cycle)
Once they reach Select, discuss co-sell on the 4 open pilots
tier_outlook: They meet everything Registered asks for. For Select they need 1 more certification (they have 9 of 10) and 1 public story (they have 0). They already meet the production requirement (2 of 2) and the region requirement (1). The review is on 31 Oct, 8 days away. The certification can be done in time. The public story is the real risk because of approval time.

headline: Kestrel's activity is going up but its results are flat: deal registrations and certifications keep rising while production deployments, usage and win rate stay flat or fall. Hold them at baseline support and tie any MDF to production deployments.
evidence: Deal registrations rose from 18 to 38 a quarter (+23% last quarter), but the 12-month win rate is only 9%. An AE notes they 'register almost every logo' and that 2 registrations this quarter overlapped our own active deals.
Production deployments are slowing: 4 in the last 12 months, but only 1 in the last 2 quarters, despite 49 certified people (12.2 certified per deployment).
Usage on partner-led customers is flat: index 100 → 101 (-2% last quarter, +1% over 3 quarters).
Pilot stall rate is 33% (2 of 6 open pilots stalled 90+ days). Applied AI support hours rose 9% to 35 with no matching increase in output.
Partner manager (Sep 15): 'Lots of activity and enthusiasm, little follow-through. They keep asking for more MDF.'
caveats: The momentum index of 8 looks positive mainly because deal registrations (+23%) and certifications (+4%) are counted alongside usage, which fell 2%. It is measuring activity, not commitment. Claude is a real 26% of their roughly 160 AI engagements and its engagements rose 5%, so this isn't a partner leaving. They've only been a partner since March 2026, so the deployment timeline may still be early, and a few of the open pilots could convert. With 1 public story they are exactly at the Select minimum, so they need to keep it.
goal: At the next regular touchpoint, agree that future MDF and Applied AI hours depend on getting stalled pilots into production, and that deal registrations must not overlap our active direct deals.
agenda: Deal-registration hygiene: settle the 2 registrations that overlapped our deals and set the rule going forward
Make MDF conditional on production deployments, not on registrations or certifications
The 2 stalled pilots: get them into production by a date or close them
Keep the public story current so they stay at Select
tier_outlook: They are safe at Select for the Oct 31 review: 49 certified (10 needed), 4 production deployments (2 needed), 1 public story (1 needed, so no margin) and 1 region. They are far from Preferred: short 51 certified, 11 production deployments and 2 public stories. At the current deployment pace, Preferred isn't realistic within the next year.

headline: Tidemark was a solid Preferred partner, but its Claude work has dropped since its Head of AI Practice left in August, so we need to find out who now owns the Claude practice this week, before the two stalled joint deals are lost.
evidence: Usage on partner-led customers fell three quarters in a row (100 → 95 → 82 → 70): down 15% last quarter and 30% overall
Claude engagements fell 41% (88 → 52 over the last two quarters), and deal registrations went 14 → 12 → 6 → 2
Only 2 production deployments in the last 2 quarters, out of 16 over 12 months. 3 of 5 open pilots have stalled for 90+ days (60% stall rate)
PM note (Sep 30): our champion, their Head of AI Practice, left in August. No replacement yet, and the practice is being folded into their data and analytics group
AE note (Oct 10): Tidemark went quiet on two late-stage joint deals, and customers say Tidemark is reassigning the delivery team
caveats: The decline started in Q1 and Q2, before the August departure, so the champion leaving may have sped up a slide that was already happening rather than caused it. The data shows 4 competitor mentions in notes over 90 days, but the notes I can see don't name a competitor, so I can't confirm a switch. Holding 168 certified people (down only 4%) and steady support hours (~70/quarter) could make the partner look healthier than it is. Those are lagging or input signals. Reassigning the delivery team may also be a normal reorg rather than a move away from Claude. Both notes are one person's read.
who: Partner manager (Marcus Lee) + regional sales VP
goal: Get the name of the new executive owner for Claude inside the merged data and analytics group, and their commitment to staff delivery on the two stalled late-stage joint deals.
agenda: Where Claude sits after the reorg: who owns the practice, and is Claude still a priority there?
The two stalled late-stage joint deals: confirm a delivery team and next steps with the customers
The 3 stalled pilots: decide which to restart with Applied AI help and which to close
Ask them directly whether they are moving work to a competitor
tier_outlook: They currently meet Preferred: 168 certified people (100 needed), 16 production deployments over 12 months (15 needed), 4 public stories (3 needed), 2 regions. Deployments have almost no margin. With only 2 in the last 2 quarters, the rolling 12-month count could drop below 15 as older deployments age out. The review on Oct 31 likely passes, but they could lose Preferred within the next 1–2 quarters unless new deployments land. Global Premier is not realistic: they are short 84 deployments, 832 certified people, 11 public stories and 1 region, and have no joint business plan.

headline: Sable & Co is a new, committed partner ramping fast (Claude is about 30% of its AI book), and the one thing between it and Select is turning its 3 open pilots into a second production deployment and a first public customer story.
evidence: Real commitment: 9 of about 30 AI engagements in the last 2 quarters ran on Claude (30% share), up from 0 in the prior 2 quarters, with a 400-person AI practice
Usage on partner-led customers rose from 100 to 170 (+70% QoQ), the strongest signal that the work is landing with customers
Certifications are matching output so far: 12 certified against 1 production deployment (12 per deployment), plus 3 open pilots with 0 stalled at 90 days
Short of Select by exactly 1 production deployment and 1 public story; certifications (12 vs 10) and regions already meet the bar
Onboarding note (2026-08-20): 'eager', building a retail and consumer practice, a dozen more architects in the certification pipeline
caveats: The base is tiny. The momentum index of 90 comes from growth off near-zero numbers (certs +200%, deal registrations 1 to 3), so it overstates how mature they are. Only one production deployment and 4 deal registrations so far, and the 50% win rate rests on very few deals. There is a single onboarding note, so we have no qualitative read on the pilots. Data mismatch: partner_since is 2026-07, but the data shows certifications, a deal registration and usage in 2026-Q2, before they joined. Either there was pre-program activity or it's an attribution error, and it should be checked. Applied AI support is 6.1 hours per engagement and rising (+75%). That is fine at this scale but worth watching as they grow.
who: Partner manager (Dana Ruiz) + Applied AI lead on the pilots
goal: Agree a dated plan to take the most advanced of the 3 open pilots into production, with that customer's commitment to a public story, so Sable qualifies for Select at the next tier review.
agenda: Go through the 3 open pilots: which is closest to production, what is blocking it, and what Applied AI help would close the gap
Find a retail or consumer customer (existing deployment or nearest pilot) willing to do a public reference, and agree who owns writing it
Be clear that the 2026-10-31 review is almost certainly out of reach; set the target as the following review
Confirm the certification pipeline (about a dozen more architects) so capacity keeps up with pilot conversion
tier_outlook: Registered, and they meet everything at that tier. For Select they already meet the certification bar (12 vs 10) and the region bar, but are short 1 production deployment (have 1, need 2) and 1 public story (have 0, need 1). The review is 2026-10-31, 8 days away, so qualifying in time is unlikely. There is no risk of losing their current tier. Realistically they can reach Select at the next review if a pilot converts and a story ships.

headline: Corbel is healthy and safely Preferred: Claude is 44% of its AI work and usage is rising. No extra outreach this cycle, but at the next QBR ask why new production deployments have slowed.
evidence: Usage on partner-led customers went up every quarter (100→112→121→130), +30% over 3 quarters and +7% last quarter
Claude is about 44% of Corbel's AI book (66 of ~150 engagements), and Claude engagements are up 6% on the prior two quarters
24 production deployments in the last 12 months from 137 certified people (5.7 certified per deployment), so certifications are turning into production work
Only 1 of 6 open pilots has stalled; deal registrations are flat at 10-11 a quarter with a 45% win rate
Oct 7 QBR note: 'Steady quarter... joint plan on track, no escalations'. Applied AI support hours are falling (60→48) while usage grows, which means Corbel is working more on its own
caveats: Only 5 of the 24 production deployments in the last 12 months came in the last 2 quarters, so roughly 19 came in the 2 before that. New production work has slowed sharply even though usage keeps rising. That isn't a risk at the Oct 31 review (24 vs. 15 needed), but if the pace stays at about 5 every 6 months, the rolling 12-month count would drop to around 10, below Preferred, within about two quarters. There is just one note, from the partner manager's own QBR, and 1 competitor mention in the last 90 days with no detail. The momentum index of 6 is a fair average here: no single input is pulling it.
who: None (Priya Shah to raise at the next regular QBR)
goal: Get a named list of which of the 6 open pilots will go into production in the next 2 quarters, to confirm the deployment slowdown is timing and not a falling pipeline.
agenda: Deployments: 5 in the last 2 quarters vs. about 19 in the 2 before. Is this timing or is the pipeline thinning?
Go through the 6 open pilots, get a target production date for each, and unblock the one that has stalled
Ask about the one competitor mention: which account it is and whether it's a real threat
Check that the joint plan targets keep the 12-month deployment count comfortably above 15
tier_outlook: Corbel clears every Preferred threshold (137/100 certified, 24/15 deployments, 4/3 public stories) and isn't at risk at the 2026-10-31 review. Global Premier is far off: it needs 863 more certified people, 76 more deployments, 11 more stories, one more region and a joint business plan, so it isn't a realistic goal soon. The main risk is the rolling 12-month deployment count if the recent slowdown continues.

headline: Ashgrove is adding certified people quickly but is not turning pilots into production: only 2 deployments in the last two quarters and 4 of 9 pilots stalled. Fix delivery conversion before giving them more support.
evidence: Certifications rose from 90 to 410 in 3 quarters (+356%), with about 150 from one bootcamp. Ashgrove could not say how many of those people work on Claude engagements (PM note, 2026-10-04).
Only 2 production deployments in the last 2 quarters, against 16 in the trailing 12 months. That works out to 25.6 certified people per deployment.
4 of 9 open pilots have stalled for over 90 days (44% stall rate). The AE says two have been open since spring and that 'marketing is ahead of delivery' (2026-09-25).
Usage on partner-led customers fell 2% last quarter (only +4% over 3 quarters), while Applied AI support hours rose 15% to 150. We are putting in more effort and getting no more usage back.
The momentum index of 19 is mostly driven by the +58% jump in certifications. Claude is about 15% of their roughly 300 AI engagements (44 Claude engagements, up 10%).
caveats: The deployment data is trailing 12 months, and Ashgrove joined in 2026-03. The 14 older deployments may be timing or attribution artifacts, which would make the recent slowdown look worse (or better) than it is. Stalled pilots can be caused by the customer (budget, security review) rather than delivery weakness. The notes cover only the AE's and PM's view, and 2 competitor mentions were logged in the last 90 days with no detail. If the newly certified staff are about to be placed on engagements, deployments could pick up next quarter.
who: Partner manager (Dana Ruiz) + Applied AI lead
goal: A written plan for each of the 4 stalled pilots, with a named Ashgrove delivery lead and target go-live date for each, agreed in exchange for continued Applied AI support.
agenda: Go through the 4 stalled pilots one at a time: what is blocking each, who owns it, and whether it is a go-live or should be closed.
Find out how many of the 410 certified people are actually staffed on Claude engagements, and name the delivery bench.
Tie Applied AI support hours to pilots moving forward, not to the number of open engagements.
Ask about the 2 recent competitor mentions and whether Claude is losing pilots to them.
tier_outlook: They meet Preferred at the 2026-10-31 review with 410 certified (100 required), 16 deployments (15 required), 3 stories (3 required) and 2 regions. But deployments and stories clear the bar by only 1 and 0, so if older deployments drop out of the 12-month window at the next review, they could fall below Preferred. Global Premier is far off: they are short 84 deployments, 12 stories, 1 region and a joint business plan. Their rising certification count should not be read as progress toward that tier.
